findings.evidence:
SELECT b~lifnr, l~name1, b~belnr, b~zfbdt, b~dmbtr
  FROM bseg AS b
  INNER JOIN lfa1 AS l ON l~lifnr = b~lifnr
  WHERE b~bukrs = @p_bukrs
    AND b~koart = 'K'
    AND b~augbl = @space
  INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE @gt_items.
findings.reason: Direct SELECT on BSEG (vendor line items) and LFA1 (vendor master). BSEG is an aggregation-based table in S/4HANA whose row structure and availability in the cloud tier must be verified; LFA1 is a classic vendor-master table. CC-02 covers BSEG/BSIK/BSAK reads; LFA1 also falls under CC-01 (SAP master-data tables). The filter `koart = 'K'` and `augbl = space` implements the open-vendor-items semantic — that business logic must be replicated when switching to released views.
findings.suggested_action: Candidate replacement: CDS view I_OperationalAcctgDocItem for open items (clearing fields expose augbl-equivalent). Join with I_Supplier (candidate for LFA1 name data). Verify both objects are released for the target product/release and carry the required fields (zfbdt/net-due-date, dmbtr, koart-equivalent) before committing. The open-item filter (augbl = space) may require a dedicated open-items entity or a filter on clearing status.
unknowns: Whether I_OperationalAcctgDocItem is released on the target product/release
Whether I_Supplier carries the NAME1 field equivalent
Whether ZFBDT (net due date) is exposed on the candidate view
Whether KOART-equivalent filtering is available in the released view
Whether open-item semantics (AUGBL = space) map directly to a clearing-status field on the released view

findings.evidence: INNER JOIN lfa1 AS l ON l~lifnr = b~lifnr
findings.reason: Direct SELECT on LFA1 (vendor master table). LFA1 is a classic SAP table; its release status in ABAP Cloud must be verified. The candidate released object is I_Supplier.
findings.suggested_action: Replace with released CDS view I_Supplier (candidate). Verify that I_Supplier is released for the target product and release, and that the required fields (name1 equivalent) are present.
unknowns: Whether I_Supplier is released on the target product/release
Exact field name mapping from LFA1-NAME1 to I_Supplier

findings.evidence:
EXEC SQL.
  UPDATE ZFI_AGING_LOG SET LAST_RUN = :sy-datum WHERE BUKRS = :p_bukrs
ENDEXEC.
findings.reason: Native SQL (EXEC SQL … ENDEXEC) is not permitted in ABAP for Cloud Development. This block also performs a direct UPDATE on table ZFI_AGING_LOG, which may be a custom Z-table; however, the approach (native SQL bypass) is the primary blocker regardless of table ownership.
findings.suggested_action: Replace with ABAP SQL (UPDATE zfi_aging_log SET last_run = @sy-datum WHERE bukrs = @p_bukrs). If ZFI_AGING_LOG is a custom table owned by the development team, a plain ABAP SQL UPDATE is sufficient. If a RAP BO governs it, use EML instead. Verify table ownership and whether a RAP BO already exists.
unknowns: Whether ZFI_AGING_LOG is a custom Z-table fully owned by the customer or a SAP-delivered object
Whether a RAP BO already governs ZFI_AGING_LOG
Database compatibility of the original native SQL syntax on the target DB

findings.evidence: DATA: gt_items TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item WITH HEADER LINE,
findings.reason: WITH HEADER LINE on an internal table is listed as obsolete syntax under CC-10. It is not allowed in the ABAP for Cloud Development language version. The implicit header line is used for field access in LOOP AT (lines 44–51) and MODIFY gt_items (line 52), and in the second LOOP AT / TRANSFER block (lines 59–63).
findings.suggested_action: Remove WITH HEADER LINE. Declare a separate work area (e.g. DATA ls_item TYPE ty_item). Change LOOP AT gt_items / MODIFY gt_items to LOOP AT gt_items INTO ls_item / modify or collect via lt_items[ ] field symbol approach. Use LOOP AT gt_items ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_item>) for in-place modification.

findings.evidence:
OPEN DATASET gv_file FOR OUTPUT IN TEXT MODE ENCODING DEFAULT.
...
TRANSFER gv_line TO gv_file.
CLOSE DATASET gv_file.
findings.reason: OPEN DATASET / TRANSFER / CLOSE DATASET access the application-server file system, which is not available in ABAP Cloud. The program writes CSV output to a hard-coded path (/usr/sap/trans/out/aging.csv) for nightly treasury pickup — this integration pattern must be replaced.
findings.suggested_action: Replace with an outbound integration mechanism: e.g. an HTTP outbound call (Communication Arrangement + CL_HTTP_CLIENT or released HTTP client class), a Business Document flow, or an event-driven pattern. The treasury system must be given a pull endpoint or receive a push notification. Exact replacement depends on the target integration architecture for the treasury system.
unknowns: Target integration architecture for the treasury system (push vs pull, protocol)
Whether a Communication Arrangement / Communication Scenario already exists for this interface
Whether the treasury system can consume an OData feed or API instead of a flat file

findings.evidence: SUBMIT zfi_treasury_upload WITH p_file = gv_file AND RETURN.
findings.reason: SUBMIT calls a classic ABAP report. Reports cannot be called in ABAP Cloud; the SUBMIT statement is not available in the ABAP for Cloud Development language version.
findings.suggested_action: Replace with a class-based call. Extract the logic of ZFI_TREASURY_UPLOAD into a released or custom class/method and call it directly, or schedule it as an Application Job using CL_APJ_RT_API. The dependency on gv_file (the CSV path) also needs to be resolved together with F-05.
unknowns: Whether ZFI_TREASURY_UPLOAD is in scope for this migration or maintained by a different team
Whether ZFI_TREASURY_UPLOAD itself has additional clean-core issues (not audited here)

findings.evidence:
* Currency conversion done in the database, native, because "it was faster"
EXEC SQL.
  UPDATE ZFI_AGING_LOG SET LAST_RUN = :sy-datum WHERE BUKRS = :p_bukrs
ENDEXEC.
findings.reason: The comment says 'currency conversion done in the database' but the actual EXEC SQL statement is a plain UPDATE to a log table — it performs no currency conversion at all. The comment contradicts the code. This could indicate missing logic (currency conversion was removed or never implemented) or a misplaced comment. No clean-core rule governs comment accuracy, so this is Unclassified, but it warrants human review.
findings.suggested_action: Clarify with the original developer: (a) Was currency conversion logic removed? (b) Is it handled elsewhere? (c) Should amounts in dmbtr be converted before bucketing or output? If conversion is needed, consider CURRENCY_CONVERSION in CDS or a released currency API.
unknowns: Whether currency conversion is expected but missing
Whether dmbtr is always in local (company-code) currency, removing the need for conversion

findings.reason: The program is a classic ABAP REPORT (executable program). While there is no explicit WRITE/ULINE/SKIP in this specific program, the REPORT statement itself signals a classic executable program structure that has no place in ABAP Cloud. The START-OF-SELECTION event block (line 27) and the PARAMETERS screen (lines 24–25) are also part of this classic paradigm. CC-09 covers the absence of list processing here; the broader program type must be replaced.
findings.suggested_action: Repackage as a RAP application job (CL_APJ_RT_API) with a selection screen equivalent implemented as job parameters, or expose the logic as an OData-based Fiori app. The bucketing and output logic become service methods.
unknowns: Whether the program is always run in background (making Application Jobs the right fit) or also interactively
